title: Synchrotron-based Photonuclear Neutron Source for Energy, Medicine and Radiation Testing
abstract: Neutron source availability is constrained by the declining number of research reactors and the challenging cost of spallation facilities, while compact accelerator-based sources remain limited to beam powers below 100~kW due to severe thermal loads from charged particle-target interactions. Here we demonstrate that synchrotron-driven photonuclear production overcomes this fundamental limitation through architectural decoupling: electrons circulating in a storage ring generate MeV-range synchrotron radiation that drives external neutron production targets, completely isolating targets from primary charged-particle power. This separation enables continuous-wave photon beam powers exceeding 200~kW per beamline while drastically reducing localized heating and reducing thermal shocks. Through systematic Monte Carlo optimization across three independent codes (OpenMC, MCNPX, FLUKA), we identify optimal target configurations delivering single-beamline neutron intensities of $3$--$13 \times 10^{14}$~n/s with inherent spectral tunability: low-Z targets (Be, D$_2$O) produce epithermal-to-thermal spectra for medical applications, while high-Z converters (W, U) generate fast neutrons for subcritical reactors.
